chunks: Abu Abdillah ibn 'Ayash said: Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tustari told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Layth al-Makki told us, saying: Abu Ishaq ibn Abdillah al-Alawi al-Uraydi told me, saying:

And the question of 'which are the days that are fasted?' was rubbed into my chest (became clear in my mind), so I headed to our Master, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), while he was in Sarba, and I did not reveal that to anyone of God's creation. So I entered upon him, and when he saw me, he said (peace be upon him): 'O Abu Ishaq, you have come to ask me about the days that are fasted, and they are four: the first is the day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab - the day God Almighty sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to His creation as 'A mercy to the worlds', and the day of his birth (peace be upon him and his family), which is the seventeenth of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal. And the day of the twenty-fifth of Dhi al-Qa'dah, on which the Ka'bah was demolished. And the day of al-Ghadir, on which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) established his brother Ali (peace be upon him) as a sign for the people and an Imam after him.' I said: 'You have spoken truly, I am your ransom; for that reason I headed [to you], I bear witness that you are God's proof against His creation.'

key_terms.حُجَّةُ ٱللَّهِ: God's proof (a title for the Imams)
key_terms.ذِي ٱلْقَعْدَةِ: The eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.رَبِيعَ ٱلْأَوَّلِ: The third month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.رَجَب: The seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.ٱلْغَدِيرُ: Al-Ghadir (the place where the Prophet appointed Ali as Imam)
key_terms.ٱلْكَعْبَةُ: The Ka'bah (the cube-shaped building in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What are the four specific days recommended for fasting in Shia tradition according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (al-Hadi), transmitted in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the theological basis for fasting on four specific days by linking them to pivotal moments in the Prophet’s life and the institution of Imamate. The Imam’s intuitive revelation to the narrator underscores the divine knowledge of the Imams, while the selection of these days—particularly the Day of Ghadir—highs the Shia emphasis on leadership (Imamah) as a core component of prophetic mission.
